details.name: Aurora 81 – Polar Landmark Tower
details.purpose: The tallest building in Aurora Haven and the symbol of its skyline: offices, a hotel, sky apartments and public sky lobbies stacked above the Aurora 81 Center.
details.feature: Named in honour of Landmark 81 in Ho Chi Minh City, its nine bundled glass tubes step back like bamboo stalks and cut blizzard wind load by about 25%. Triple-glazed solar glass, piles that keep the permafrost frozen and heat recovered from lifts and exhaust air make it a net-zero-energy tower.

details.name: Aurora 81 Crown & Spire
details.purpose: The top of Aurora 81: a glass-walled public sky deck, a glowing LED crown and the communication spire that tops the city skyline.
details.feature: The spire carries mobile and emergency-radio relays, aircraft warning lights and a wind sensor that feeds the city's blizzard alerts. Through the polar night the crown glows in aurora colours, and it turns red to warn the whole city when a blizzard is on its way.

details.name: Smart Mast-Arm Traffic Signal
details.purpose: Overhead traffic signals that control the downtown junctions for cars, trams, buses and people on foot, each with a lit street-name sign.
details.feature: An AI camera adjusts green times to the real traffic and gives instant priority to ambulances, trams and buses. Heated LED lenses never ice over in a blizzard, and a battery backup keeps every junction working through a power cut.

details.feature: An AI camera adapts green time to real traffic and gives priority to ambulances and buses; a battery backup keeps the signals running through blackouts.

details.name: Smart Pedestrian Signal
details.purpose: Pedestrian lights at the four crossings around the Central Interchange Station, where Aurora Avenue meets Glacier Avenue and the metro entrances bring the biggest crowds downtown.
details.feature: Thermal sensors spot people waiting, so nobody has to take off a glove to press a button. The green phase stretches automatically for older people, wheelchairs and prams, and in a white-out the signal beeps and a guide strip in the heated kerb vibrates to lead people across.

details.name: Smart Pedestrian Signal
details.purpose: Tells people when it is safe to cross Aurora Avenue and Glacier Avenue at the Central Interchange.
details.feature: Push-free sensor detects waiting pedestrians; countdown light and pedestrian warning sign; extra-long green for elderly people.

details.name: Air Base Control Tower
details.purpose: The glass-cab control tower of Aurora Air Base, where controllers guide every military take-off, landing and rescue flight.
details.feature: Radar and thermal cameras let controllers see the whole runway in polar night and white-outs. It shares one live airspace picture with the Compact Polar Airport tower, so civil and military flights never cross, and it can take over the airport's traffic if that tower ever goes offline.

details.name: Air Base Control Tower
details.purpose: 12 m tower with a glass cab that guides every take-off and landing at Aurora Air Base.
details.feature: Radar dish and weather sensors on the roof; controllers can see the whole runway even in polar night thanks to thermal cameras.

details.name: Aurora Metro Monorail – Glacier Line
details.purpose: A driverless four-car train of the Glacier Line, the east–west metro line, leaving the Central Interchange Station eastbound towards East Gallery Avenue with commuters, shoppers and stadium fans.
details.feature: The line runs deep underground, so even a 120 km/h blizzard never stops it; trains come every 4 minutes and every 90 seconds after big events at the Aurora Snow Stadium. Braking energy is fed back to the line, and the heated cars have space for wheelchairs, prams and skis.

details.name: Aurora Metro Monorail – Glacier Line (running)
details.purpose: 4-car electric monorail running eastbound between Central Interchange Station and Glacier Mall Station.
details.feature: Driverless electric monorail (front car, 2 passenger cars, end car) gripping a single guideway beam: silent, cannot derail, regenerative brakes return 30 % of the energy to the grid; heated cars with wide doors, wheelchair spaces and ski racks.

details.name: Aurora Metro Monorail – Aurora Line
details.purpose: A driverless four-car train of the Aurora Line, the north–south metro line, waiting at the Central Interchange Station to carry passengers under the city centre.

Heated cars with wide doors, wheelchair spaces and ski racks come every 3 minutes at rush hour, and in an emergency the line becomes a warm shuttle to the shelters.

details.name: Glacier Line Monorail Guideway – Sector 1/8

details.name: Downtown Robotaxi & Electric Delivery Van – Sector 1/2
details.purpose: A self-driving electric taxi and an electric delivery van on the downtown streets: robotaxis take residents door to door, and the vans restock the shops, cafés and the supermarket.
details.feature: Robotaxis are booked by app and shared by riders going the same way, so the city needs very few private cars. Delivery vans work mostly at night when the streets are empty and carry heated cargo boxes that stop fresh food freezing at -45 °C; both charge at the EV & Hover-Car Charging Hub.

details.name: Downtown Electric Traffic
details.purpose: Electric taxis, cars and delivery vans driving through the new downtown.
details.feature: All vehicles are zero-emission and share live traffic data with the AI Control Tower.

details.name: North Haven Avenue & Turning Circle
details.purpose: The northern avenue from the city centre to the science quarter, the Polar Rescue and Resilience Station and the Northern Renewable Park, used by residents, researchers and emergency crews.
details.feature: A heated pedestrian crossing never ices over, the turning circle is wide enough for fire engines and tracked rescue vehicles to turn without reversing, and paired LED lanterns brighten as people approach, keeping the route safe through the polar night.

details.purpose: Links the city centre with the Science & Rescue Campus and the Polar Rescue and Resilience Station.
details.feature: The northern continuation of Aurora Avenue, with a marked crossing and a turning circle at its end.

details.name: Aurora 81 Plaza
details.purpose: The public square at the foot of Aurora 81, with a fountain, flagpoles, benches and evergreen trees, where office workers, residents and tourists meet.
details.feature: Granite paving warmed by return water from the district-heating loop stays ice-free even at -45 °C, and evergreen windbreaks calm the gusts. In deep winter the fountain basin is frozen into a small free skating rink lit by warm LEDs.

details.name: Red & Yellow Monument Flower Beds
details.purpose: Red and yellow flowers, the colours of the Vietnamese national flag, framing the President Ho Chi Minh Monument on its island in the middle of the Aurora Roundabout.
details.feature: The flowers are raised in the Evergreen Greenhouse Dome and planted in boxes warmed by district-heating pipes, under clear frost covers that open on mild days. Soil sensors water them with recycled snowmelt, and evergreen shrubs keep the beds green while the flowers are changed each season.

details.name: Red & Yellow Flower Beds and Solar Lanterns
details.purpose: Flowers in the colours of the national flag decorate the monument all year round.
details.feature: Cold-hardy flowers from the city greenhouses grow in heated planter boxes under clear frost covers, watered with recycled snow-melt and replanted each season; four solar lanterns, topped up from the city grid during the polar night, light the statue after dark.

details.name: Black Granite Pedestal
details.purpose: The base of the President Ho Chi Minh Monument: it lifts the statue so it can be seen from all four avenues and carries the memorial inscription.
details.feature: The memorial inscription "CHỦ TỊCH HỒ CHÍ MINH (1890 - 1969)" in raised silver letters is softly lit so it can be read all through the polar night. Heating cables under the stone platform melt ice so visitors and ceremony guards never slip, and sealed granite resists frost cracks.

details.name: Black Granite Pedestal
details.purpose: Raises the statue so it can be seen from all four avenues and carries the memorial inscription.
details.feature: Front panel with raised silver letters 'CHỦ TỊCH HỒ CHÍ MINH (1890 - 1969)'; polished dark granite with light stone base, corner pilasters and cornice; slate platform covers the whole island.

details.name: Northern Lights School & Botanical Conservatory
details.purpose: The city's main primary and secondary school, for about 900 pupils aged 6 to 18, facing Liberty Mall, with a glass botanical conservatory where pupils have science lessons and families visit at weekends.
details.feature: During the polar night lessons start later and daylight-spectrum lighting keeps pupils alert. LED grow lights and heat recovered from the classrooms keep the conservatory green all year, and a protected stairway leads straight down to the Medical & School Shelter.

details.name: Northern Lights School & Botanical Conservatory
details.purpose: Primary and secondary school campus with a glass botanical conservatory dome for science lessons.
details.feature: LED grow lights and heat recovered from the school keep the conservatory green through the polar night, so pupils can study living plants all year.

details.name: Northern Lights School & Botanical Conservatory
details.purpose: Primary and secondary school campus with a glass botanical conservatory dome for science lessons.
details.feature: LED grow lights and heat recovered from the school keep the conservatory green through the polar night, so pupils can study living plants all year.

details.name: Igloo Fresh Supermarket & Food Hall
details.purpose: Downtown's main supermarket and food court on Liberty Mall, where residents do their weekly shopping and office workers, students and shoppers eat lunch.
details.feature: About half of what it sells is made in the city: protein bread, noodles and drinks from the Snow-to-Food & Water Plant and vegetables and fish from the Evergreen domes. Refill stations cut packaging, heat from its CO₂ fridges warms the food hall, and its food waste becomes biogas.

details.name: Igloo Fresh Supermarket & Food Hall
details.purpose: The city's main grocery hall and food court, with a cold-storage wing.
details.feature: Zero plastic packaging and CO2 heat-recovery refrigeration.

details.name: Aurora Cinema & Performing Arts Center
details.purpose: The city's cinema and theatre on Liberty Mall, showing films, concerts, ballet, school shows and festivals for residents and tourists.
details.feature: Its main hall can turn into a "polar night sky" dome for aurora and space films, and the daylight-lit foyer café helps people through the dark months. Timber-lined halls give warm acoustics, and heat recovery reuses the audience's own body warmth to heat the building.

details.name: Aurora Cinema & Performing Arts Center
details.purpose: Stepped theater complex with a wide ground-level lobby and taller auditorium core.
details.feature: Cross-laminated timber lines the auditorium for warm acoustics and keeps the cold out.

details.name: Aurora Observatory
details.purpose: A public observatory for watching the northern lights, stars and planets, and the source of the city's daily aurora forecast.
details.feature: A heated dome shutter never freezes while the telescope stays at outdoor temperature for sharp images. Through the two months of polar night it hosts free stargazing evenings, and its live forecast pings the spa's Aurora Eye and the city's photo tours as soon as the sky lights up.

details.name: [Northern Renewable Park] Ice-Proof Wind Farm – Sector 1/2
details.purpose: The wind farm of the Northern Renewable Park: two rows of ice-proof turbines along the windy northern edge, producing about 60 MW of clean power, most of it in the stormy winter months.
details.feature: Heated blades and AI yaw control keep them turning in freezing fog, and the rows are offset so no turbine stands in another's wake. Above 90 km/h the blades feather and lock to ride out 120 km/h blizzards, and the east end stays clear of the airport's approach path.

details.name: [Northern Renewable Park] Bifacial Solar Farm – Sector 1/2
details.purpose: Long rows of double-sided solar panels facing the low southern sun, in front of the Aurora Horizon Lookout; in the two midnight-sun months they produce power 24 hours a day.
details.feature: Bright snow reflects light onto the panel backs for about 25% more output, and a steep tilt with heated frames lets snow slide off. The summer surplus charges the battery bank and heat storage, and a central spine road lets service vans reach every row.

details.name: [Northern Renewable Park] Water Recycling Line – 1 Snowmelt & Greywater Intake
details.purpose: The first stage of the city's water recycling line: it collects used greywater from homes, showers and laundries, plus meltwater from the cleared-snow melt fields.
details.feature: Both inlets arrive in insulated mains laid below the frost line, and a basin warmed by district-heating return water keeps the inflow liquid at -45 °C. Smart flow meters spot leaks in the city's pipes, helping Aurora Haven recycle about 95% of its water.

details.name: Meltwater Intake Basin
details.purpose: Receives snowmelt and greywater before treatment.
details.feature: Heated floor; level sensors call the pumps.

details.name: Greywater Main Inlet
details.purpose: Brings greywater from the city sewers.
details.feature: Buried below the frost line.

details.name: Process Water Pipe
details.purpose: Carries the water on to the next treatment stage.
details.feature: Insulated and heat-traced so it never freezes.

details.name: Snowmelt Inlet
details.purpose: Brings meltwater from the snow-melt fields.
details.feature: Buried below the frost line.

details.name: Process Water Pipe
details.purpose: Carries the water on to the next treatment stage.
details.feature: Insulated and heat-traced so it never freezes.

details.name: [Northern Renewable Park] Water Recycling Line – 2 Intake Pumps & Bar Screen
details.purpose: Lifts the incoming water into the recycling line and screens out grit, sand and debris before treatment.
details.feature: Variable-speed pumps run on wind and solar power and slow down when flows are low to save energy. Self-cleaning screens never clog, and the washed grit is reused as anti-slip sand on the city's icy footpaths.

details.name: Intake Pump & Screen
details.purpose: Pumps and screens the raw water.
details.feature: Variable-speed pumps run on wind power.

details.name: Process Water Pipe
details.purpose: Carries the water on to the next treatment stage.
details.feature: Insulated and heat-traced so it never freezes.

details.name: [Northern Renewable Park] Water Recycling Line – 3 Settling Basins
details.purpose: Two settling basins in series where the water rests so that suspended solids sink to the bottom.
details.feature: Slow scraper bridges push the settled sludge to a hopper, and the sludge is piped to the biogas digester to make clean gas instead of waste. Insulated covers stop the basins from freezing, and the clear water spills over the rim weirs to the filters.

details.name: Process Water Pipe
details.purpose: Carries the water on to the next treatment stage.
details.feature: Insulated and heat-traced so it never freezes.

details.name: Settling Basin (Clarifier)
details.purpose: Lets fine particles settle out of the slowly moving water.
details.feature: A heated air film over the water stops ice forming.

details.name: Scraper Bridge
details.purpose: Turns slowly and scrapes the settled sludge to the centre.
details.feature: The sludge goes to the biogas digesters.

details.name: Bridge Drive
details.purpose: Turns the scraper bridge.
details.feature: One revolution an hour.

details.name: [Northern Renewable Park] Water Recycling Line – 4 Sand & Membrane Filters
details.purpose: Sand and membrane filter vessels polish the settled water, removing fine particles and most bacteria.
details.feature: Half the filters work while the other half back-wash, so the flow never stops, and the back-wash water returns to the start of the line, so not a drop is wasted. Pressure sensors tell operators exactly when each membrane needs cleaning.

details.name: [Northern Renewable Park] Water Recycling Line – 6 Recycled Water Tower
details.purpose: Stores the clean recycled water and feeds the city's service-water mains for toilets, laundries, street cleaning, greenhouse irrigation and fire hydrants.

details.name: Northern Energy Garden
details.purpose: A small public garden beside the battery bank, the grid substation and the geothermal plant, where residents and school groups learn about the city's clean energy.
details.feature: Its Energy Hub board shows live output from fusion, wind, solar, geothermal and batteries, so visitors can see where the city's power is coming from at that moment. Warm benches face the hub, and signs lead to the Northern Renewable Park.

details.name: Circular Recycling Center
details.purpose: The city's materials hub, where residents and businesses bring glass, metal, plastics, electronics and batteries to be sorted, repaired or turned back into raw materials.
details.feature: AI optical sorters and robot arms handle about 30 tonnes a day; batteries that have finished their second life in the battery bank are dismantled and their lithium goes to the fusion fuel-cycle plant. Food scraps go to the biogas digester and only true leftovers to the Plasma Waste Converter.

details.name: Snow Owl Eco-Home
details.purpose: A passive-house family home in the quiet western eco-homes neighbourhood, home to a family of four.
details.feature: Thick super-insulated walls, triple glazing and an airtight shell mean it needs about 80% less heat than an ordinary house; on most days the warmth of the family, the cooking and the appliances almost heats it by itself.

details.name: Arctic Fox Kindergarten
details.purpose: The kindergarten of the western eco-homes neighbourhood, caring for about 30 toddlers and pre-schoolers from nearby families and from Aurora Air Base and Polar Garrison staff.
details.feature: A glazed winter-garden playroom lets children play with sand and plants even at -45 °C, and a snow yard sheltered by the windbreak pines has a warm-up hut. Because many parents work shifts at the air base, it stays open from 6 am to 8 pm.

details.name: Polar Bear Eco-Home
details.purpose: A larger family home in the western eco-homes neighbourhood for parents, three children and a grandmother.
details.feature: The family's electric car doubles as a backup battery that can power the house through a blackout, and a steep, smooth roof sheds heavy snow before it can overload the structure. A ground-floor granny flat with its own entrance keeps the grandmother close but independent.

details.name: Seal Eco-Home
details.purpose: A compact, step-free eco-home in the western neighbourhood for an older couple who want to live independently.
details.feature: Wide doorways, a walk-in shower and lever handles make daily life easy, a heated airlock porch keeps the icy wind out, and a telecare button links the couple to Snowflake General Hospital. A built-in cupboard holds 72 hours of emergency food and water.

details.name: Aurora Snow Stadium – Sector 1/5
details.purpose: The city's main outdoor arena, with about 8,000 seats, for snow football, bandy, school sports days and the Midwinter Aurora Festival held during the polar night.
details.feature: Seats and stairs are warmed by the district-heating loop, while the canopy and wind screens keep blizzards off the crowd; LED floodlights allow matches in the two dark months, and the snow pitch is groomed with snow made from recycled water. It is also the east side's emergency assembly point.

details.name: President Ho Chi Minh Monument
details.purpose: The heart of the Aurora Roundabout and of the city: residents and visitors come here to honour Uncle Ho, hold flag-raising ceremonies and meet on national holidays.
details.feature: Inspired by the statue in front of Ho Chi Minh City Hall, the brushed stainless-steel figure of Uncle Ho waving to the people is softly floodlit through the polar night. Recovered heat keeps the platform free of ice, and the city's guided walking tours start here.

details.name: President Ho Chi Minh Monument
details.purpose: The heart of Aurora Roundabout: residents and visitors come here to remember Uncle Ho, hold flag-raising ceremonies and meet on national holidays.
details.feature: Uncle Ho stands waving to the people, modelled on the statue in front of Ho Chi Minh City Hall and rendered as a faceted sculpture of silver-grey stainless-steel blocks; the base plate is heated by waste heat so ice never builds up, and four solar lanterns at the corners of the platform, topped up from the city grid in the polar night, light it after dark.

details.feature: Uncle Ho stands waving to the people, modelled on the statue in front of Ho Chi Minh City Hall and rendered as a faceted sculpture of silver-grey stainless-steel blocks; the base plate is heated by waste heat so ice never builds up, and four solar lanterns at the corners of the platform, topped up from the city grid in the polar night, light it after dark.

details.feature: Uncle Ho stands waving to the people, modelled on the statue in front of Ho Chi Minh City Hall and rendered as a faceted sculpture of silver-grey stainless-steel blocks; the base plate is heated by waste heat so ice never builds up, and four solar lanterns at the corners of the platform, topped up from the city grid in the polar night, light it after dark.

details.feature: Uncle Ho stands waving to the people, modelled on the statue in front of Ho Chi Minh City Hall and rendered as a faceted sculpture of silver-grey stainless-steel blocks; the base plate is heated by waste heat so ice never builds up, and four solar lanterns at the corners of the platform, topped up from the city grid in the polar night, light it after dark.

details.feature: Uncle Ho stands waving to the people, modelled on the statue in front of Ho Chi Minh City Hall and rendered as a faceted sculpture of silver-grey stainless-steel blocks; the base plate is heated by waste heat so ice never builds up, and four solar lanterns at the corners of the platform, topped up from the city grid in the polar night, light it after dark.

details.feature: Uncle Ho stands waving to the people, modelled on the statue in front of Ho Chi Minh City Hall and rendered as a faceted sculpture of silver-grey stainless-steel blocks; the base plate is heated by waste heat so ice never builds up, and four solar lanterns at the corners of the platform, topped up from the city grid in the polar night, light it after dark.

details.name: Snowflake General Hospital
details.purpose: Aurora Haven's main hospital, with about 250 beds, a 24-hour emergency department, surgery, maternity and children's wards for residents, tourists and polar expeditions.
details.feature: Telemedicine links its doctors with specialists worldwide, and light-therapy rooms treat winter depression. Medical oxygen comes from the food plant's electrolysers and liquid helium for the MRI scanners from the fusion station, and the shelter below keeps patients safe in any disaster.

details.name: Aurora Line Entrance Flag
details.purpose: Tall red flags beside the Central Interchange Station entrances, so passengers can spot the metro from far down the avenue, even in falling snow.
details.feature: Each flagpole carries an LED beacon and a Bluetooth signal that guides phones and smart canes of blind passengers to the entrance in a white-out. The cold-proof recycled fabric stays flexible and does not tear even in 120 km/h winds.

details.name: Outdoor Bio-Fuel Heater
details.purpose: A warming fire basket beside the heated bus stop on the edge of Aurora 81 Plaza, where people waiting outdoors and plaza visitors can warm their hands.
details.feature: It burns clean biogas from the Biogas Tank, made from the city's food scraps, so it adds no fossil carbon. A presence sensor lights it only when people are nearby, and it shuts off by itself in strong wind.

details.name: Reindeer Sled Team
details.purpose: Fuel-free reindeer sled rides for tourists and families, starting near the observatory and heading out along the tundra trails.
details.feature: The reindeer are cared for by local herders who follow Sámi herding traditions; rides are limited to a few hours a day to protect the animals, and GPS collars let the herders find them quickly when they graze out on the tundra.

details.name: Garrison and Stadium Road Connections – Sector 1/7
details.purpose: Western Garrison Avenue and Eastern Stadium Avenue, the extensions of Glacier Avenue that link downtown with the Polar Garrison in the west and the Aurora Snow Stadium in the east.
details.feature: Heated lanes stay open even in 120 km/h blizzards, so both avenues double as the city's main evacuation and emergency routes. On match days smart signs open an extra bus lane to the stadium, and storm-rated lanterns light the crossings at the garrison gate and the stadium approach.

details.feature: Paired LED fixtures powered by the wind farm; heated glass never ices over.

details.name: Polar Garrison Military District – Sector 1/7
details.purpose: The headquarters of the Polar Garrison: command centre, barracks, training and logistics for the soldiers who defend Aurora Haven and support search-and-rescue and disaster relief.
details.feature: Its pavilions stand on raised frames above the permafrost and are joined by enclosed, heated links, so personnel never have to cross open ground in a blizzard. The observation tower watches the western approaches, and in a disaster the garrison's vehicles, stores and field kitchens support the city.

details.name: Polar Vehicle Maintenance Hangar
details.purpose: Shelters military support vehicles and maintenance equipment.
details.feature: The service hangar is separated from the accommodation wings and faces a clear equipment apron.

details.name: Vehicle Service Apron
details.purpose: Heated apron where the supply craft is loaded and serviced.
details.feature: Under-surface heating keeps it free of ice; it opens straight onto the maintenance hangar doors.

details.name: Polar Garrison Supply Craft
details.purpose: VTOL cargo craft that flies personnel and stores to remote polar outposts.
details.feature: The supply craft has a dedicated service apron beside the maintenance hangar.

details.name: Garrison Boundary Rail
details.purpose: Defines the edge of the platform or reserved compound.
details.feature: Open rail sections preserve visibility and leave the designated entry gaps clear.

details.name: Garrison Supply Store
details.purpose: Stages maintenance and logistical stores beside the service hangar.
details.feature: A compact supply rack stands on the equipment side of the compound, clear of the arrival route.

details.name: Observation Tower Platform

details.feature: Carries the observation cabin; the access ladder ends here.

details.name: Garrison Observation Cabin

details.name: Garrison Communications Unit

details.feature: A compact roof-mounted unit serves the observation point.

details.name: Observation Tower Access Ladder
details.purpose: Provides a service-access route to the observation platform.
details.feature: The vertical ladder follows the side of the braced tower frame and reaches the raised platform.

details.name: Aurora 81 Center (Podium Mall)
details.purpose: The five-level shopping podium at the base of Aurora 81: shops, a fresh-food supermarket, a food court and the tower's main lobby, serving the whole southern district.
details.feature: A glass atrium roof and daylight-spectrum lighting keep it bright through the polar night; the shops are heated by waste heat from the tower and the supermarket fridges, and a heated tunnel to the Aurora 81 Residences means nobody has to step outside in a blizzard.

details.feature: They glow dim and warm when the street is empty and brighten as people or vehicles approach, saving about 70% of the energy and keeping the sky dark enough to see the aurora. Each pole also measures air quality and snow depth for Aurora Core.

details.name: Aurora Air Base Runway – Sector 1/3

details.feature: Heated asphalt with de-icing pipes on the district-heating loop stays clear of ice, and AI-guided landing lights work in white-out blizzards. If the civil airport is ever closed, it serves as the city's backup runway, so supply flights can still land.

details.name: Aurora Civic Center & Municipal Hall
details.purpose: The town hall of Aurora Haven beside Aurora Roundabout, where the mayor and city council meet and residents come for ID cards, permits, housing and family services.
details.feature: A one-stop service hall and city app settle most requests in a single visit, and every year residents vote online on how part of the city budget is spent. Snow-pine roof terraces insulate the building, and the Aurora Core Command Bunker beneath it can run the whole city if the surface is cut off.

details.name: Snowmelt and Heat Recovery Works
details.purpose: Melts the dirty snow ploughed off the streets and car parks of the eastern districts, using the last useful heat in the district-heating water before it flows back to the fusion station.
details.feature: Snowplows tip into a melt basin warmed by the loop's return water, so heat that would be wasted clears the streets; the meltwater is screened and stored in insulated tanks as fire-fighting water for the Industry Park, then sent to the Water Recycling Line. Street snow never enters the drinking-water plant.

details.name: Snowmelt Collection Basin
details.purpose: Heated basin where snowplows tip snow cleared from the streets.
details.feature: Warm return water piped under the basin floor melts the snow; grit settles out before the water goes to treatment.

details.name: Insulated Water Storage
details.purpose: Insulated tanks that store treated meltwater for street cleaning, fire hydrants and irrigation.
details.feature: Foam-insulated, trace-heated walls keep the water above freezing; level sensors report to Aurora Core.

details.name: Insulated Water Storage
details.purpose: Insulated tanks that store treated meltwater for street cleaning, fire hydrants and irrigation.
details.feature: Foam-insulated, trace-heated walls keep the water above freezing; level sensors report to Aurora Core.

details.name: Heat Recovery Module
details.purpose: Heat exchanger that passes the fusion station's spent cooling water under the melt basin.
details.feature: Reuses heat that would otherwise go to the dry cooling towers.

details.name: Water Treatment Service House
details.purpose: Filter hall and control room of the snowmelt works.
details.feature: Sand filters and UV lamps clean the meltwater; operators watch the basin and tanks from a warm control room.

details.name: Insulated Transfer Pipe
details.purpose: Carries filtered meltwater from the treatment house to the storage tanks.
details.feature: Pre-insulated, heat-traced pipe that never freezes, kept inside the fenced service yard.

details.name: Heat Recovery Link
details.purpose: Carries warm return water from the heat exchanger to the melt basin.
details.feature: A short insulated loop inside the service yard.

details.name: Storage Balancing Link
details.purpose: Links the two storage tanks so they fill and drain evenly.
details.feature: A motorised valve can isolate either tank for cleaning.

details.name: Polar Science Courtyard – Sector 1/4
details.purpose: The green courtyards and footpaths of the Knowledge Quarter, where students, researchers and visitors rest between lectures and walk to the institutes and transit stops.
details.feature: Paths and benches sit over the district-heating return pipes, so the courtyard stays usable at -45 °C. Raised planters show hardy arctic plants with QR-code labels, and a sheltered corner is used as an outdoor classroom for snow and weather experiments.

details.name: Polar Rescue and Resilience Station
details.purpose: The city's fire, rescue and disaster-response headquarters: home of the fire brigade, ambulance and ice-rescue teams, and of the 112 emergency centre that dispatches fire, ambulance and police.
details.feature: A heated hangar keeps fire engines, tracked rescue vehicles and the vertical take-off Polar Emergency Shuttle ready to leave within 60 seconds. Its own battery reserve and satellite terminal keep it running if the grid or networks fail, and it runs the drills for the city's underground shelters.

details.name: Polar Rescue Operations Base
details.purpose: Base for blizzard response, search teams and emergency supplies.
details.feature: An insulated hangar faces the city approach, with a separate craft bay and a communications mast.

details.name: Rescue Shuttle Apron
details.purpose: Heated apron where the rescue shuttle stands ready.
details.feature: Heated surface keeps the apron free of ice for emergency take-offs.

details.name: Polar Emergency Shuttle
details.purpose: Electric VTOL shuttle that flies supplies and people out when snow blocks the roads.
details.feature: Ducted fans cope with strong crosswinds; the heated apron and battery warmers let it launch within minutes.

details.name: Blizzard Communications Mast
details.purpose: Weather and radio mast of the rescue station.
details.feature: Measures wind and snowfall on site and relays storm alerts between rescue teams and Aurora Core.

details.name: Emergency Satellite Terminal
details.purpose: Backup satellite link for the rescue station.
details.feature: Keeps rescue teams connected if fibre and mobile networks fail; stands clear of the shuttle apron.

details.name: Emergency Energy Reserve
details.purpose: Battery reserve that keeps the rescue base running in a blackout.
details.feature: Second-life battery modules sit away from the public approach and can run the hangar, lights and radios for two days.

details.name: Terrace Safety Rail

details.name: Aurora Snow Garden Park
details.purpose: A quiet public park at the foot of Mount Aurora on the southern edge of the city, where residents walk, picnic in the midnight-sun months and meet friends after a spa visit.
details.feature: Snow-capped rocks and winter pines shelter the paths from the wind, and benches with heated seats stay warm even at -45 °C. In winter the snow is groomed into a sledging slope and a lantern-lit snow-sculpture trail for families from Snowpine Residences.

details.name: Polar Climate & Ice Research Institute
details.purpose: A research institute that studies ice, permafrost, climate change and polar wildlife, and shares its data with scientists worldwide.
details.feature: Self-driving drones from its hangar scan the ice and tundra every day, and a -30 °C cold lab keeps fresh samples before they go to the Ice Core Archive. Its field data feed the blizzard forecasts of Aurora Core and the long-term climate plans of the city.

details.name: Satellite Communication Dish
details.purpose: Receives weather and ice data from satellites and links the city to the world through low-orbit satellite internet.
details.feature: Its heated, snow-shedding dish keeps working in blizzards, and it is the city's backup link whenever the main fibre cable is cut, so the hospital, airport and rescue station always stay online.

details.name: Weather Sensor Station
details.purpose: An automatic weather station that measures wind, temperature, snow depth and visibility around the clock.
details.feature: It sends data every minute to the Aurora Core AI, which issues blizzard warnings, adjusts the district-heating loop and tells the airport and air base when to de-ice; a built-in battery keeps it reporting through power cuts.

details.name: Polar Scientist
details.purpose: Researchers from the Polar Climate & Ice Research Institute collecting ice and snow samples on the edge of the city.
details.feature: Heated smart suits adjust to body temperature automatically, satellite beacons connect them to the Polar Rescue and Resilience Station, and every core they drill is logged by GPS for the Ice Core Archive.

details.name: Geothermal Power Plant
details.purpose: Turns heat from deep under the plateau into clean electricity and hot water around the clock, working with the fusion station as the second heat source for the district-heating loop.
details.feature: Lithium is extracted from the hot brine for the fusion station's breeding blanket, and the cooled brine is pumped back underground together with captured CO₂, which turns to stone in the basalt, so the plant has a negative carbon footprint.

details.name: Evergreen Greenhouse Dome
details.purpose: Grows fresh salad, tomatoes, peppers, herbs and berries all year, so residents eat fresh vegetables even in the polar night and in winters when supplies can only arrive by air.
details.feature: Heated by the district-heating loop and wrapped in thermal curtains at night; LED grow lights give the plants 18-hour "days" on stacked hydroponic racks that use 90% less water than fields, and CO₂ from the biogas plant and the waste converter boosts growth.

details.name: Evergreen Aquaponics Dome
details.purpose: A fish-and-vegetable farm where tanks of Arctic char and rainbow trout feed beds of lettuce, herbs and strawberries; its fish go fresh to the Northern Fish Market.
details.feature: Fish waste becomes fertiliser for the plants and the plants clean the water for the fish, so the loop loses under 2% of its water a day; pure oxygen from the food plant's electrolysers keeps the fish healthy, and sensors adjust feeding, light and temperature automatically.

details.name: EV & Hover-Car Charging Hub
details.purpose: The east side's heated garage and charging station for electric cars, delivery vans, taxis and hover-cars, used by plant workers, stadium visitors and residents.
details.feature: Heated indoor bays keep batteries warm at -45 °C so they charge fast and keep their range; wireless pads start charging as soon as a car parks, and at busy times parked cars can feed power back to the grid. Bays are booked by app and every kilowatt is zero-carbon.

details.name: Metro Entrance – Central Interchange Station
details.purpose: The two main street entrances of the Central Interchange Station on Liberty Mall, with escalators down to the Aurora Line and on to the deeper Glacier Line.
details.feature: Double airlock doors and a warm-air curtain keep the cold out of the station, and the heated steps never ice. Screens show live train times and how full each train is, and in an emergency the entrances lead straight down to the underground shelters.

details.name: Metro Lift Entrance – Glacier Line (Deep Level)
details.purpose: Glass lift pavilions beside Glacier Avenue that take passengers straight down to the deep Glacier Line platforms of the Central Interchange Station.
details.feature: They give step-free access for wheelchairs, prams, luggage and older passengers: the fast lifts reach the platform in about 20 seconds, the heated pavilions double as warm waiting rooms, and battery backup keeps the lifts running in a power cut.

details.name: Emergency Hatch – Aurora Core Command Bunker
details.purpose: The street-level escape hatch of the Aurora Core Command Bunker under the Civic Center, used by city leaders and emergency teams if the main entrances are blocked.
details.feature: Its heated, blast-proof frame never freezes shut and opens from both sides; a flashing beacon and GPS transmitter guide rescuers to it even when it is buried under drifting snow.

details.name: Fresh-Air Intake – Aurora Core Command Bunker
details.purpose: Brings fresh outdoor air down to the command bunker so the city's emergency team can keep working underground for weeks.
details.feature: A heated cap stops snow and ice from blocking it, filters remove smoke, dust and chemicals, and a heat-recovery unit warms the -45 °C air with the bunker's outgoing air before it reaches the rooms.

details.name: Emergency Hatch – Medical & School Shelter
details.purpose: The emergency exit to the street from the Medical & School Shelter beneath Snowflake General Hospital and the Northern Lights School.
details.feature: It is wide enough for a stretcher and has a built-in hoist, so patients can be lifted out safely; its heated frame never freezes shut, and pupils practise this evacuation route twice a year.

details.name: Fresh-Air Intake – Medical & School Shelter
details.purpose: Supplies clean, fresh air to the shelter where hospital patients, staff and schoolchildren take refuge in an emergency.
details.feature: Hospital-grade filters and slightly higher air pressure inside keep smoke and germs out, and battery-backed fans keep the air moving even in a total blackout, so surgery can continue safely underground.

details.name: Emergency Hatch – Food Reserve Bunker
details.purpose: The street-level emergency exit of the Food Reserve Bunker, the underground store that holds 30 days of meals and drinking water for every resident of Aurora Haven.
details.feature: Heated seals stop the hatch freezing shut, and it can be opened by hand from inside with no power. A beacon and strobe light guide rescue teams to it in a white-out, and it is opened and tested in the city's monthly shelter drills.

details.name: Fresh-Air Intake – Food Reserve Bunker
details.purpose: The ventilation stack that brings filtered outdoor air into the Food Reserve Bunker and keeps its stores cool and dry.
details.feature: A heated, snow-proof cap and dust and gas filters keep the air clean even in a blizzard. In winter the stack draws in polar air as free refrigeration, holding the food stores at a steady 4 °C with very little power.

details.name: Emergency Hatch – Residential Emergency Shelter
details.purpose: A hand-operated exit from the Residential Emergency Shelter, where downtown families can live safely with bunks, water and power during a disaster or an extreme blizzard.
details.feature: The heated hatch never freezes shut, opens by hand from inside if the power fails and reports its status to the Polar Rescue and Resilience Station. A GPS beacon and strobe guide rescuers straight to it in a white-out.

details.name: Fresh-Air Intake – Residential Emergency Shelter
details.purpose: The fresh-air stack of the Residential Emergency Shelter, supplying clean, warm air to the families sheltering below.
details.feature: Incoming air passes through filters and a heat-recovery unit warmed by the outgoing air, keeping the shelter at about 18 °C on very little power, and CO₂ sensors adjust the airflow to the number of people inside.

details.name: Heated Bus Shelter
details.purpose: Glass shelters at the downtown stops where passengers wait warm and dry for the electric buses and trams.
details.feature: Glass walls block the wind and an infrared heater on clean grid power switches on when someone steps inside. Screens show live arrival times, and an emergency call button connects straight to the city's 112 emergency centre.

details.name: Bus Shelter Bench
details.purpose: A seat inside each heated bus shelter for older passengers, parents with small children and anyone waiting for the bus.
details.feature: The seat is gently heated only while someone is sitting on it, saving energy, and a built-in charging point tops up phones, whose batteries drain fast in deep cold.

details.name: Eco-Tour Guide
details.purpose: Leads visitors around the Northern Renewable Park, the Water Trail, the observatory and the best aurora-watching spots.
details.feature: Speaks five languages and uses an AI translation headset for the rest, carries a satellite emergency beacon on every trip, and runs tours by reindeer sled or electric snow-bus.

details.name: Pocket-Plaza Bench
details.purpose: Benches in the small pocket plazas at the corners of the Liberty Mall blocks, where people rest, wait for friends or eat a snack outdoors on milder days.
details.feature: The seats are warmed by district-heating return water that has already heated the shops around them, so they stay ice-free at no extra energy cost. Tough recycled plastic will not crack in the cold, and each bench is a stop on the Liberty Mall audio walking tour.

details.name: Greenhouse Farmer
details.purpose: One of the growers who plant, tend and harvest the crops and fish in the Evergreen domes and guide school groups around them.
details.feature: Wears a heated thermal suit for the walk between domes and uses a tablet linked to AI crop sensors to control light, water, nutrients and temperature for every growing bed.

details.name: Recycling Worker
details.purpose: Works at the Circular Recycling Center, supervising the sorting line and helping residents at the drop-off and reuse counter.
details.feature: Robot arms do the heavy lifting while the worker checks the AI sorting results and repairs old skis, coats and electronics for the reuse shop; a heated thermal suit makes work in the outdoor yard safe in deep cold.

details.name: Resident in a Smart Thermal Suit
details.purpose: A resident walking through downtown on the way to work, school, the shops or the metro.
details.feature: The smart thermal suit heats itself from a small battery, warns the wearer of frostbite risk and sends an automatic SOS with their location to the Polar Rescue and Resilience Station after a fall in the snow.

details.name: Aurora 81 Sky Garden
details.purpose: Evergreen planters on a high sky terrace overlooking Aurora 81 Plaza, a green rest spot for office workers and hotel guests of the Aurora 81 District.
details.feature: Dwarf pines grow in heated planters behind glass wind screens, watered by drip lines with recycled water. They give birds a stepping stone across the city and offer a sheltered view of the northern lights high above the street.

details.name: Rooftop Evergreen Planter
details.purpose: Heated planter of dwarf pines on the roof terrace.
details.feature: Insulated box with a heated root zone so the pines survive the polar winter.

details.name: Aurora Snow Stadium – Silver Rib Storm Shell
details.purpose: The outer skin of silver ribs that wraps the whole stadium and shields the stands and entrances from wind and drifting snow.
details.feature: Recycled-aluminium ribs lean outwards to break 120 km/h blizzard winds into a gentle breeze inside the bowl and shed snow away from the doors; built-in LED strips glow in team colours or aurora green and double as emergency exit lighting.

details.name: Silver Ribbed Stadium Shell
details.purpose: Outer skin of silver ribs that wraps the whole stadium, inspired by Valencia's new stadium.
details.feature: Recycled aluminium ribs lean outwards to shelter the entrances from snow and wind; LED strips can light it in team colours.

details.name: Long-Range Air Surveillance Radar
details.purpose: A long-range radar that watches the sky up to 400 km around the city, tracking aircraft and approaching storms.
details.feature: It warns of storm fronts, guides lost aircraft home and spots threats early; a heated radome never ices up, its picture is shared with the civil airport and Aurora Core, and a battery backup keeps it watching through power cuts.

details.feature: Warns of storms, lost aircraft and threats; runs on the base grid with its own battery backup.

details.name: Heat Storage Tank
details.purpose: Stores hot water from the geothermal plant and the fusion station for the city's district-heating loop.
details.feature: Vacuum insulation loses less than 1% of its heat per day; the tank charges when demand is low and releases heat at the morning and evening peaks, and it can keep homes warm for about 12 hours if a heat source stops.

details.name: Biogas Tank
details.purpose: Stores the biogas made in the digester beside the recycling center from food scraps collected from homes, restaurants and the food plant's kitchen.
details.feature: The cleaned biogas fuels the outdoor bio-fuel heaters downtown and standby generators for the emergency shelters; its CO₂ is piped to the greenhouse domes and the leftover digestate becomes fertiliser, so food scraps never reach a landfill.

details.name: Kids' Snowman
details.purpose: Snowmen built by children of the western eco-homes and the Arctic Fox Kindergarten.
details.feature: Each polar night the neighbourhood holds a snowman contest lit by warm lanterns; the snowmen stand until the spring thaw, when their meltwater flows to the city's water recycling line.

details.name: Kids' Snowman

details.name: Western Windbreak Pine
details.purpose: A tall pine in the green buffer between the Polar Garrison and the eco-homes that slows the icy west wind blowing into the city.
details.feature: It belongs to a planted windbreak belt that cuts wind speed by up to 40% in its shelter, saving heating energy for the homes and the kindergarten behind it.

details.name: Carbon-Monitoring Tree
details.purpose: A sensor tree in the western green buffer that absorbs CO₂ and measures how much carbon and clean air the city's trees provide.
details.feature: A trunk sensor records its growth and carbon storage, and a small air monitor reports CO₂ and air quality to the city's open climate dashboard, helping planners choose the best trees for the polar climate.

details.name: Wildlife Shelter Tree
details.purpose: A snow-laden tree in the western green buffer where snow buntings, ptarmigans and arctic hares shelter from the wind.
details.feature: Nest boxes and a motion-triggered camera let the Polar Climate & Ice Research Institute and local schoolchildren count the wildlife visiting the edge of the city.

details.name: Energy Hub Snow Pine
details.purpose: A small pine beside the heat storage tank that softens the energy hub for people walking by.
details.feature: Its soil box is warmed by spare heat from the geothermal plant, so the roots never freeze, and it is watered with recycled water from the Northern Renewable Park.

details.name: North Downtown Windbreak Pine
details.purpose: One of the tall snow pines planted in rows across the northern districts of downtown to slow the icy north wind before it reaches the streets.
details.feature: The belt stops the north wind before it can funnel between the towers, making the walk to the metro noticeably warmer, and it catches drifting snow before it can bury the roads.

details.name: Carbon-Capture Grove
details.purpose: A grove of hardy trees in the western green buffer that absorbs CO₂ and screens the eco-homes from the air base.
details.feature: Planted in compost from the Circular Recycling Center, the trees lock carbon into wood and soil, catch drifting snow and dampen aircraft noise before it reaches the homes.

details.name: North Downtown Street Pine
details.purpose: One of the small snow pines along the streets of the northern downtown districts that keep the city green all year.
details.feature: Soil cells under the pavement give the roots room to grow and store snowmelt for the short summer, and the pines filter dust and soften traffic noise along the busy streets.

details.feature: The trees are stepping stones in a green chain that links the open tundra with the city's gardens. Roads beside the corridor have dimmed night lighting and wildlife underpasses, so animals can cross safely.

details.name: Slow Down Sign – Stadium Area
details.purpose: Warns drivers to slow down near the Aurora Snow Stadium, where big crowds cross the road on match days.
details.feature: A solar-powered flashing LED sign with a radar display that shows each driver's speed; linked to the city's traffic AI, it lowers the limit to 20 km/h automatically whenever a match or festival is on.

details.name: Slow Down Sign – Stadium Area
details.purpose: Warns drivers to slow down before the Aurora Snow Stadium, where big crowds cross on match days.
details.feature: Reflective orange warning sign with a solar flashing LED; a small radar shows each driver their speed.

details.name: Slow Down Sign – Eco-Homes Residential Zone
details.purpose: Warns drivers to slow to 30 km/h as they enter the eco-homes neighbourhood with its families and the Arctic Fox Kindergarten.
details.feature: A solar-charged flashing LED and a speed display show each driver their speed, and the sign flashes more strongly at kindergarten drop-off times and in white-out conditions.

details.name: Slow Down Sign – Eco-Homes Residential Zone
details.purpose: Warns drivers to slow down to 30 km/h before the Eco-Homes, a quiet family neighbourhood.
details.feature: Reflective orange warning sign with a solar flashing LED; a small radar shows each driver their speed.

details.name: Slow Down Sign – Roundabout Ahead
details.purpose: Warning signs on the avenues approaching the Aurora Roundabout, telling drivers to slow down for the President Ho Chi Minh Monument, pedestrians and trams.
details.feature: A solar-charged flashing LED and a radar speed display show each driver their speed. The sign flashes faster when road sensors detect black ice or a white-out, and it sends speed data to Aurora Core to make the junction safer.

details.name: Glacier Line Tunnel Floor
details.purpose: The waterproof base slab of the deep east–west Glacier Line tunnel, carrying the guideways, walkways and platforms.
details.feature: Thick insulation under the slab stops the tunnel's warmth from thawing the permafrost below, and side drains carry any seepage to the city's water recycling line, so the floor stays dry and ice-free all year.

details.name: Glacier Line Tunnel Floor
details.purpose: Waterproof concrete base slab of the deep east–west metro tunnel (56 m long).
details.feature: Heated slab with side drains keeps the tunnel dry and free of ice even at -40 °C outside.

details.name: Glacier Line Insulated Tunnel Wall – Sector 1/8
details.purpose: The insulated concrete walls of the Glacier Line tunnel, lined with cream panels and a gold guide stripe that leads passengers to the exits and shelters.
details.feature: Thick insulation keeps the tunnel at about +5 °C all winter. The walls are blast-proof, and doorways in them open straight into the four downtown emergency shelters, so people reach safety without going outside.

details.feature: Thick insulation keeps the tunnel at +5 °C all winter; openings lead to lifts and civil-defence shelters.

details.name: Glacier Line Track Buffer Stop – Sector 1/2
details.purpose: Hydraulic buffer stops at both ends of the Glacier Line, where the turn-back sidings end and trains reverse for the return journey.
details.feature: If a train ever overran, the hydraulic buffers would absorb its energy and stop it gently. Track sensors also brake driverless trains automatically several metres before the buffer, so it is a last line of safety.

details.name: Aurora Line Tunnel Floor
details.purpose: The waterproof base slab of the shallow north–south Aurora Line tunnel under Aurora Avenue, carrying the guideways and walkways on either side of the Central Interchange Station.
details.feature: It rests on insulated, air-cooled foundations that keep the permafrost frozen, while the slab itself is gently warmed by district-heating return water, so meltwater never turns to ice on the track.

details.name: Aurora Line Tunnel Floor
details.purpose: Waterproof concrete base slab of the shallow north–south metro tunnel (56 m long).
details.feature: Heated slab with side drains keeps the tunnel dry and free of ice even at -40 °C outside.

details.name: Aurora Line Insulated Tunnel Wall – Sector 1/4
details.purpose: The insulated walls of the Aurora Line tunnel, with cream panels and the same gold guide stripe as the Glacier Line, so passengers always know the way.
details.feature: Lying just below the street, the tunnel is wrapped in thick insulation that keeps it at about +5 °C when it is -45 °C outside. Acoustic panels soak up train noise, and openings lead to the lifts and the emergency shelters.

details.name: Aurora Line Insulated Tunnel Wall
details.purpose: Insulated concrete walls lined with cream panels and a gold guide stripe.
details.feature: Thick insulation keeps the tunnel at +5 °C all winter; openings lead to lifts and civil-defence shelters.

details.name: Polar Snow Ground
details.purpose: The packed snow ground between the streets, plazas and districts of Aurora Haven, where children play and residents ski or walk across town.
details.feature: It lies over insulation boards and gravel drainage that stop frost heave from damaging nearby roads, and groomers reopen ski and snowshoe tracks across it after every snowfall, linking homes, schools and parks.

details.name: Polar Snow Ground
details.purpose: Packed snow ground that covers the open land between the streets, plazas and districts of Aurora Haven.
details.feature: Laid over gravel fill, drains and insulation boards that stop frost heave; ploughs keep the roads and plazas clear while the snow around them stays.

details.name: [Compact Polar Airport] Heated Runway & Departing Dreamliner – Sector 1/4
details.purpose: Aurora Haven's air link to the world: the heated highway from downtown and the main runway, where Flight VN-81, a Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, is taking off. In deep winter all supplies arrive by air.
details.feature: District-heating pipes under the 2,800 m runway and the highway keep them free of snow and ice without de-icing chemicals; an all-weather landing system and LED approach lights allow landings in the polar night and in white-outs, and aircraft refuel with synthetic e-kerosene, not fossil fuel.

details.name: Underground Metro & Emergency Shelters – Sector 4/4

details.name: [Mount Aurora] Ama Dablam-Style Snow Peak & Hanging Glacier – Sector 1/6
details.purpose: Mount Aurora, the city's 35-metre landmark peak shaped like Nepal's Ama Dablam, with a long eastern and a shorter western shoulder. Inside its snow and rock lies the four-level Mount Aurora Geothermal Spa Resort, found in no other city.
details.feature: Its deep snow cover works as a natural blanket that holds in the spa's geothermal heat. Radar and strain sensors watch the snow load day and night and release it safely before an avalanche can build, and lights behind the blue-ice "Aurora Pendant" glacier make the peak the city's southern beacon.

details.name: [Mount Aurora] Foothill Pines, Moraine Boulders & Snowbanks – Sector 1/8
details.purpose: A sheltering belt of arctic pines, glacial boulders and snowbanks around the foot of Mount Aurora that protects the spa grounds from wind and drifting snow.
details.feature: The pines on the south, east and west sides work as a living snow fence, while the city-facing side stays open to the view. The clean snow they trap is collected in calm weeks for the Snow-to-Food & Water Plant, and the boulders give shelter to arctic hares and snow buntings.

details.name: [Mount Aurora] North Portal, Forecourt & Boulevard
details.purpose: The main entrance of the spa resort: a short tree-lined boulevard from the Mount Aurora Approach, a drop-off loop for the spa shuttle and a heated granite forecourt.
details.feature: The forecourt and benches are warmed by the spa's used hot water, so guests walk ice-free from the shuttle to the door. A thermal revolving door and an air curtain open into a rock-cut entrance grotto that keeps the -45 °C air out and the warm, humid spa air in.

details.name: [Mount Aurora] Aurora Lagoon – Outdoor Geothermal Mineral Pool
details.purpose: An open-air silica mineral pool at the north-east foot of the peak, kept at 38 °C, where residents and tourists bathe under the northern lights or the midnight sun.
details.feature: Silica-rich overflow from the indoor Mineral Lake keeps it at 38 °C with no chemicals, and the cooled water returns to the geothermal loop. Heated larch boardwalks keep bare feet off the ice, and a covered warm passage leads bathers straight back inside the mountain when a blizzard rolls in.

details.name: [Mount Aurora] Insulated Rock Shell & Glass Lift Core
details.purpose: The structure inside Mount Aurora: four stepped spa levels at 0, 4.5, 9 and 13.5 m inside a reinforced, insulated rock shell, linked by a panoramic glass lift.
details.feature: The super-insulated shell keeps the spa at a steady 28 °C while it is -45 °C outside, and ventilated piles stop its warmth from thawing the permafrost. The lift has an enclosed fire-safe stair, and in a city-wide emergency the heated levels can serve as a warm refuge for up to 1,000 people.

[Mount Aurora – Level 2] Volcanic Mud Terraces
details.purpose: The mud-therapy floor at 4.5 m: a shared 8 × 10 m warm mud field, private mud basins, mineral rinse showers and heated drying loungers that relax muscles and soothe skin.

[Mount Aurora – Level 4] Summit Sanctuary & Aurora Eye

Liberty Mall – Monument Promenade
details.purpose: The tree-lined pedestrian promenade through the four central blocks of downtown, framing the view from the President Ho Chi Minh Monument to Mount Aurora; it hosts festivals, markets and parades.

[Snow-to-Food & Water Plant – Stage 1] Snow Harvest & Melt Hall
details.purpose: Receives clean, wind-packed snow that electric harvesters gather from drifts on the open tundra upwind of the city, and melts about 3,000 tonnes a day into raw water – the first step of the city's drinking water and food.
details.feature: The melt pits sit under a warm-water main that brings about 14 MW of spare heat from the fusion station, so the snow does the job of a cooling tower; a crusher and conveyor feed the pits, a clarifier settles out grit, and the stockpile bay keeps the plant running through about 10 calm days.

details.name: [Snow-to-Food & Water Plant – Stage 2] Drinking-Water & Mineral Works
details.purpose: Turns the meltwater into about 2,500 m³ of safe drinking water a day – all of the city's tap water – and purifies the mineral salts that the food lines need.
details.feature: Membrane filters and UV light remove every germ, then calcite beds add calcium and magnesium for taste, health and pipe protection; online sensors test the water every five minutes, and the insulated reservoir holds two days of supply in case of a breakdown.

details.name: [Fusion Power Station – Stage 1] Heavy-Water Separation Works
details.purpose: Extracts deuterium – heavy hydrogen, the first of the two fusion fuels – from the deuterium-rich water left in the food plant's electrolysers and purifies it into reactor-grade heavy water.
details.feature: Snowmelt holds only about 28 g of deuterium per cubic metre, but the reactor burns only about 70 g a day; isotope-exchange columns and vacuum distillation raise it to 99.8% purity, so the city's fuel literally falls from the sky as snow.

details.name: [Fusion Power Station – Stage 2] Lithium Blanket & Tritium Fuel-Cycle Plant
details.purpose: Prepares the lithium salt that breeds tritium – the second fusion fuel – inside the reactor's blanket, recycles unburned fuel and collects the helium "ash".
details.feature: The blanket breeds slightly more tritium than the reactor burns, so none is ever imported; its lithium comes from geothermal brine and recycled batteries, all tritium work is sealed in gloveboxes, and the recovered helium – about a litre of liquid helium a day – keeps the hospital's MRI scanners cold.

details.name: [Fusion Power Station – Stage 3] Fusion Core – Compact D-T Tokamak
details.purpose: The heart of "the city's own sun": a compact tokamak whose superconducting magnets hold a 150-million-degree plasma where deuterium and tritium fuse into helium, giving about 800 MW of heat.
details.feature: It runs on about 170 g of fuel a day and turns less than one gram of matter into energy, exactly as E = mc² predicts; it makes no CO₂ and no long-lived waste, and if anything fails the plasma simply goes out in a split second – it cannot melt down or run away.

details.purpose: The station's main control room, staffed day and night, with a public gallery where students and tourists learn how fusion powers and heats Aurora Haven.
details.feature: Operators and an AI "digital twin" watch thousands of sensors and can stop the plasma in milliseconds; the gallery looks straight at the reactor dome, and a live wall map shows where the station's power and heat are flowing in the city right now.

details.name: Visitor Forecourt
details.purpose: Paved forecourt of the control & visitor centre.
details.feature: Heated paving.

details.feature: Glazed on both long sides.
