details.name: Aurora Core – AI Control Tower
details.purpose: The city's operations centre in the Polaris Quarter, where engineers and an AI "digital twin" of Aurora Haven run traffic, heating, power, snow clearing and emergency alerts.
details.feature: The AI forecasts blizzards up to 48 hours ahead, then pre-warms roads, reroutes buses and alerts every phone. Its data centre's waste heat flows into the district-heating loop, and the command bunker under the Civic Center takes over if the tower ever goes offline.

details.name: Polaris Green Office Tower
details.purpose: A high-rise office tower in the Polaris Quarter for clean-energy, engineering and software companies that work with the fusion station and the renewable park.
details.feature: Solar glass on its sunny faces makes electricity, most of all in the 24-hour daylight of summer, and heat from computers and people is recovered to warm the floors. Staff book desks by app, so empty floors drop to low heat automatically.

details.name: Ice Crystal Apartments
details.purpose: A residential skyscraper in the Polaris Quarter with about 350 apartments for families and couples, a few minutes' walk from the metro, the university and the shops.
details.feature: Every flat has an enclosed glass winter-garden balcony that stays usable at -45 °C and acts as a warm buffer for the wall behind it. A shared daylight lounge on the top floor helps residents through the polar night.

details.name: Northern Lights Sky Lofts
details.purpose: Loft apartments in the Polaris Quarter for young professionals and couples, with open-plan homes and a shared rooftop terrace.
details.feature: A heated, glass-screened roof deck is the quarter's best spot to watch the aurora, and on aurora nights the building's outdoor lights dim automatically. A heat-recovery facade reuses the warmth of the flats' exhaust air.

details.name: Frostline Co-Living Tower
details.purpose: Affordable co-living for newcomers, young workers and visiting researchers: private studios with shared kitchens, lounges, laundry and a gym.
details.feature: Shared kitchens and appliances cut energy use per person by about a third. A heated store for bikes, sleds and skis sits by the entrance, and weekly community dinners cooked with food from the Snow-to-Food plant help newcomers make friends during the long dark.

details.name: Aurora Haven Police Headquarters
details.purpose: The city's central police station, whose 24-hour police control room works side by side with the 112 emergency centre at the Polar Rescue and Resilience Station to send patrols across Aurora Haven.
details.feature: Officers patrol on electric snowmobiles and in heated electric cars, and thermal cameras linked to Aurora Core spot anyone collapsed in the snow before hypothermia sets in. It also commands the Southside Police & Mountain Rescue Post.

details.name: Golden Aurora Senior Residences
details.purpose: Assisted-living apartments for about 150 older residents who want a home of their own with care close at hand, in the heart of downtown near the metro.
details.feature: Heated corridors lead from every flat to a ground-floor day centre with meals, physiotherapy and a hair salon, so residents never have to go out in the cold. A smart-watch alarm calls the on-site nurses at any hour, and doctors from Snowflake General Hospital visit twice a week.

details.name: [Polaris Quarter] Street Lanterns, Snow Spruces & Street Life
details.purpose: The heated sidewalks and central courtyard of the Polaris Quarter, with lanterns, snow spruces, log benches, a warm fountain and residents out walking among the towers.
details.feature: Spruces around the towers break the strong gusts that high-rises create at street level. The courtyard fountain runs on warm district-heating water so it never freezes, and wireless pads under the parking bays charge electric cars.

details.name: Arctic University – Main Hall
details.purpose: The main building of Arctic University, with lecture halls and offices for about 5,000 students of polar engineering, fusion energy, food science, medicine and climate science.
details.feature: Students train on the city's real systems – the fusion station, the Snow-to-Food plant and the renewable park – and lectures are streamed live to remote polar stations. Its great lecture hall doubles as a warm public refuge in emergencies.

details.name: Aurora Public Library
details.purpose: The city's free public library, with books, study rooms, a children's corner and computers for residents of all ages.
details.feature: During the polar night it stays open 24 hours as a bright, warm "living room" for the city, with daylight-lamp reading rooms. Its library of things lends out skis, snowshoes, telescopes and light-therapy lamps, so residents share instead of buying.

details.name: Polar Science & Climate Center
details.purpose: A hands-on science museum and planetarium where schoolchildren, residents and tourists learn about the polar climate, the northern lights and how Aurora Haven lives without fossil fuels.
details.feature: A live data wall shows the city's power, heat and water flows in real time, and the planetarium dome recreates the aurora on cloudy nights. Interactive exhibits explain fusion and the Snow-to-Food plant, and entry is free for school classes.

details.name: Snowflake Bookshop & Café
details.purpose: A cosy bookshop and café on the university avenue where students and residents buy books, read and meet over hot drinks.
details.feature: A trade-in shelf gives readers credit for their old books, keeping paper in use. Heated window seats and a dark-season book club with live video talks by authors keep it lively through the polar night.

details.name: Permafrost Research Institute
details.purpose: A university institute that studies the frozen ground under Aurora Haven and designs foundations that keep it frozen as the climate warms.
details.feature: It watches thousands of temperature sensors in the piles of every building and road and warns engineers before the ground starts to thaw or heave. New foundation designs are tested in its cold laboratory before they are used in the city.

details.name: Ice Core Archive
details.purpose: A deep-freeze library of ice cores drilled from polar glaciers, kept for scientists who read thousands of years of climate history trapped in the ice.
details.feature: The vaults stay at -30 °C, cooled for most of the year simply by drawing in polar outdoor air; in summer heat pumps take over and pass their heat to the district-heating loop. A viewing window lets visitors see the ancient ice.

details.name: Student Residence Hall
details.purpose: A residence hall with about 120 rooms for university students, a two-minute walk from the lecture halls, the library and the metro.
details.feature: Study lounges and kitchens are open 24 hours, rent includes a free metro and tram pass, and smart meters let each floor compete to save the most energy, with a prize every month.

details.name: [Knowledge Quarter] Street Lanterns, Snow Spruces & Street Life
details.purpose: The busy university avenue of the Knowledge Quarter, where students and researchers walk between lectures under lanterns and snow spruces.
details.feature: Each lantern has a free Wi-Fi hotspot and an emergency call button, and its sensors record air quality and snowfall for students' research projects. The sidewalks are kept clear for wheelchairs and bikes all winter, and the spruces shelter walkers from the wind.

details.name: Aurora Language School
details.purpose: Teaches English, Vietnamese, Norwegian and other languages to newcomers, international researchers, students and residents of all ages.
details.feature: New residents get free classes for their first six months, so everyone can join city life quickly. AI tutors let learners practise speaking at any hour, and evening classes are streamed for shift workers at the fusion station and the food plant.

details.name: Campus Health Clinic
details.purpose: A small walk-in clinic for students, university staff and nearby residents, offering check-ups, minor treatment, vaccinations and counselling.
details.feature: It specialises in polar health: vitamin-D tests, frostbite care and help with winter depression. Online booking and a video link to Snowflake General Hospital let patients see a specialist without crossing town in a blizzard.

details.name: Northern Maths & Robotics Lab
details.purpose: A makerspace where school pupils and university students learn maths, coding and robotics in after-school clubs and project teams.
details.feature: Teams build real robots for the city, such as small snow-clearing robots and crawlers that inspect district-heating pipes, and the 3D printers use plastic recycled at the Circular Recycling Center.

details.name: Faculty Housing
details.purpose: A house of furnished flats for visiting professors, lecturers and their families, a short walk from the campus.
details.feature: A welcome host helps visiting scholars settle in, and flats are let for a term or a year, so no home stands empty. Smart thermostats on the district-heating loop warm each flat only when it is occupied, and a heated shed stores skis and sleds.

details.name: Little Auroras Kindergarten
details.purpose: A kindergarten beside the Knowledge Quarter for about 40 under-sixes, many of them children of university staff, students and downtown workers.
details.feature: A heated indoor play hall with a sandpit and climbing wall lets children run and play through the polar night, and a sheltered snow garden is used whenever it is warmer than -25 °C. Parents collect their children with a secure check-out app.

details.name: Aurora Observatory Annex
details.purpose: The downtown branch of the Aurora Observatory, where forecasters track the northern lights and space weather and school classes come for astronomy lessons.
details.feature: It sends aurora alerts to residents' phones and warns the power grid, airport and radio services when a solar storm could disturb power lines, GPS and communications. Public telescopes are set up outside on clear winter nights.

details.name: [Knowledge Quarter] Street Lanterns, Snow Spruces & Street Life
details.purpose: The busy university avenue of the Knowledge Quarter, where students and researchers walk between lectures under lanterns and snow spruces.
details.feature: Each lantern has a free Wi-Fi hotspot and an emergency call button, and its sensors record air quality and snowfall for students' research projects. The sidewalks are kept clear for wheelchairs and bikes all winter, and the spruces shelter walkers from the wind.

details.name: Polar Trade Center
details.purpose: The business centre where Aurora Haven's companies meet buyers from abroad and sell polar know-how, from cold-proof batteries to snow-to-food technology.
details.feature: It hosts the yearly Arctic Tech Expo, and virtual-reality showrooms let foreign buyers tour products without flying in. A customs and export office clears air cargo for the airport.

details.name: Aurora Green Finance Hall
details.purpose: A public green bank that funds the city's clean-energy and climate projects and helps residents invest in them.
details.feature: Residents can buy small community shares in the wind and solar farms and earn a yearly dividend. A public screen in the hall shows how much CO₂ every funded project saves.

details.name: Arctic Stock Exchange
details.purpose: The digital stock exchange of the polar region, where shares in Arctic companies, green bonds and carbon credits are traded.
details.feature: Its servers are cooled for free by polar air and their heat is fed into the district-heating loop. Trading runs fully online, and a visitors' gallery and school classes show students how markets work.

details.name: Northwind Insurance
details.purpose: Insures homes, vehicles, businesses and expeditions against the risks of polar life, from frozen pipes to blizzard damage.
details.feature: Weather-sensor data triggers automatic payouts after a severe blizzard, with no paperwork, and homes fitted with smart leak and frost sensors pay lower premiums because problems are caught early.

details.name: Tundra Capital Offices
details.purpose: Offices of a venture-capital firm and start-up incubator that invests in new polar and clean-technology companies founded in Aurora Haven.
details.feature: Two floors of free incubator space give student start-ups from Arctic University desks, mentors and seed funding. A heated, snow-shedding crown stops ice from falling onto the sidewalk below.

details.name: Polar Credit Union
details.purpose: A member-owned community bank where residents save, borrow and get free financial advice.
details.feature: It offers low-interest loans for home insulation, heat pumps and electric vehicles, and its heated 24-hour service lobby doubles as a safe shelter for anyone caught in the cold.

details.name: Aurora Business Hotel
details.purpose: A business hotel with about 180 rooms and conference halls for engineers, scientists and business visitors.
details.feature: Blackout blinds and body-clock lighting help guests adjust to the polar night or the midnight sun, and an electric shuttle runs to the airport every 20 minutes. Its conference hall hosts the city's international science and business meetings.

details.name: Fjord Logistics & Central Post Office
details.purpose: The headquarters of the company that runs the city's air-cargo supply chain, with the central post office for letters and parcels on the ground floor.
details.feature: In deep winter, when supplies can only arrive by air, its planners schedule every cargo flight with Aurora Core. Heated parcel lockers across the city open 24 hours, and electric vans and delivery drones bring parcels overnight.

details.name: Snowline Courthouse & Law Chambers
details.purpose: The city court, where judges hear civil and criminal cases, together with offices for lawyers, notaries and free legal advice.
details.feature: Video hearings let people at remote stations and the airport take part without travelling, and a free legal-aid desk helps residents with housing and work questions.

details.name: [Financial District] Street Lanterns, Snow Spruces & Street Life
details.purpose: The heated sidewalks and courtyard of the Financial District, with lanterns, snow spruces and log benches; in the polar night it hosts a Christmas market with a decorated tree and stalls of mulled berry juice, gingerbread and handmade ornaments.
details.feature: The market stalls plug into clean power points instead of diesel generators, and the ornaments are crafted from recycled glass and wood. Snow-melting sidewalks stay ice-free for the crowds.

details.name: Christmas Market – Mulled Berry Juice Stall
Snowcap Bakery
details.purpose: A neighbourhood bakery on West Market Street baking fresh bread, cinnamon buns and Vietnamese bánh mì from early morning.
details.feature: Its flour blends starch and protein flour from the Snow-to-Food & Water Plant, so the city's bread does not depend on imported grain. Heat from the electric ovens warms the shop, and unsold bread goes to the community fridge every evening.

details.name: Reindeer Café
details.purpose: A cosy café on West Market Street serving coffee, cloudberry tea and hot chocolate; the downtown reindeer-sled loop starts at its door.
details.feature: Its dairy-style milk comes from precision fermentation at the Snow-to-Food plant, with no cows needed. A heated window bar lets guests watch the sled set off, and coffee grounds are collected as compost for the greenhouse domes.

details.name: Frostbite Noodle House
details.purpose: A noodle restaurant on West Market Street serving Vietnamese phở, ramen and hot noodle soups that warm up workers, students and families.
details.feature: The noodles are made with starch from the Snow-to-Food plant and the fresh herbs come from the Evergreen greenhouse dome all year. Takeaway goes out in returnable bowls on heated e-cargo bikes.

details.name: Aurora Night Market Hall
details.purpose: A small covered market hall on West Market Street where about a dozen stalls sell street food, local crafts and fresh produce late into the evening.
details.feature: Stalls are booked night by night through an app at low rent, so new small businesses can start easily. A heated floor and an air curtain keep it warm when the doors open, and it is busiest in the polar night when people want light and company.

details.name: Polar Pharmacy
details.purpose: The pharmacy of West Market Street, selling medicines, vitamins and first-aid supplies and giving health advice.
details.feature: Open 24 hours, it gives free vitamin-D advice for the dark months, and a robot dispenser fills prescriptions sent directly by doctors. Housebound residents can receive their medicines by delivery drone.

details.name: Northern Fish Market
details.purpose: A fish shop on West Market Street selling fresh Arctic char and rainbow trout from the Evergreen Aquaponics Dome, plus smoked fish and seafood soups.
details.feature: All fish is farmed in the city's own clean aquaponics loop, so no wild fish stocks are harmed. In winter its cold store is chilled with outdoor air, and fish scraps go to the Biogas Tank.

details.name: Mitten & Scarf Boutique
details.purpose: A knitwear shop on West Market Street selling mittens, scarves, hats and sweaters for polar winters.
details.feature: Yarn is spun from recycled wool and reindeer fibre, and its heated mittens recharge by USB. A mitten-swap shelf lets children trade outgrown gloves, and a free knitting circle meets every week through the polar night.

details.name: [West Market Street] Street Lanterns, Snow Spruces & Street Life
details.purpose: Street life on the southern half of West Market Street: lantern-lit pavements, snow spruces, a parked electric car and residents out shopping and meeting friends.
details.feature: Shop awnings drain meltwater into heated gutters instead of onto shoppers, and the lanterns flash amber when a blizzard warning is issued. Short-stay charging bays let electric cars top up while their owners shop.

details.name: Hot Chocolate House
details.purpose: A small chocolate café in a timber house on West Market Street, making its own chocolates and serving hot chocolate, soups and waffles to shoppers and families.
details.feature: Its drinking chocolate uses dairy-style milk from the Snow-to-Food & Water Plant. As one of the city's official "warm points", it keeps a heated corner with blankets and a first-aid kit open to anyone caught in a blizzard, day or night.

details.name: Tundra Grocery
details.purpose: A neighbourhood grocery store on West Market Street, so residents of the street and nearby Snowpine Residences can buy their daily food within a five-minute walk.
details.feature: Refill shelves sell flour, protein mince and bottled water from the Snow-to-Food & Water Plant and fresh greens from the Evergreen domes. Older residents can order by app and have their shopping brought to the door by electric cargo sled.

details.name: Lantern Tea Room
details.purpose: A tea room serving teas, dumplings and pastries to West Market Street shoppers, with rental flats on the upper floors.
details.feature: Its glazed sun-room front catches every hour of the low winter sun, and each polar night it hosts the street's lantern festival. Heat recovered from the kitchen helps warm the flats upstairs.

details.name: Sauna Supply Co.
details.purpose: Sells, installs and repairs home saunas, heaters and bath products for residents who keep warm and healthy through the polar night.
details.feature: Its smart sauna heaters run on the city's clean electricity and warm up when power is cheapest, during the windiest hours of the Northern Renewable Park. Old heaters are taken back and recycled at the Circular Recycling Center.

details.name: West Market Fire & Ambulance Station
details.purpose: The downtown fire and ambulance station, a branch of the Polar Rescue and Resilience Station, covering West Market Street, the Polaris Quarter, Liberty Mall and Snowpine Residences.
details.feature: Heated engine bays keep an electric fire engine, an ambulance and a tracked snow-rescue vehicle ready to leave within 60 seconds, so crews reach any downtown address in about 4 minutes. Firefighters also teach free first-aid and blizzard-safety classes.

details.name: Cloudberry Patisserie
details.purpose: A patisserie with apartments above, known for its cloudberry tarts and birthday cakes, which also bakes snacks for the Pinecone Kindergarten.
details.feature: Cloudberries are grown in the Evergreen domes and frozen at harvest, so the tarts are made all year. Waste heat from the electric ovens warms the apartments upstairs, and unsold cakes are shared each evening through a food-sharing app.

details.name: [West Market Street] Street Lanterns, Snow Spruces & Street Life
details.purpose: Street life on the southern half of West Market Street: lantern-lit pavements, snow spruces, a parked electric car and residents out shopping and meeting friends.
details.feature: Shop awnings drain meltwater into heated gutters instead of onto shoppers, and the lanterns flash amber when a blizzard warning is issued. Short-stay charging bays let electric cars top up while their owners shop.

details.name: Aurora Glacier Mall & Crystal Atrium
details.purpose: The largest shopping mall downtown, on East Gallery Avenue, with fashion and household shops, a food court, an indoor playground and a glass-roofed atrium garden.
details.feature: The Crystal Atrium is an indoor park with real trees and daylight-spectrum lighting, open to everyone as a warm place to walk in the polar night. Waste heat from the shops' fridges and lights warms the building, and a heated covered walkway leads to the tram stop.

details.name: Aurora Modern Art Gallery
details.purpose: The city's contemporary art gallery on East Gallery Avenue, showing works by Arctic and Vietnamese artists, light installations and photography.
details.feature: In its immersive light room, visitors' movements paint the walls with aurora colours. Entry is free during the polar night, and resident artists run workshops on making art from recycled materials.

details.name: Iceberg Coworking Hub
details.purpose: A shared office on East Gallery Avenue where freelancers, remote workers and small start-ups rent desks and meeting rooms by the hour.
details.feature: Working close to home cuts commuting in deep cold, and hourly booking means unused rooms stay on low heat. Fast satellite and fibre internet, a podcast studio and daylight lamps at every desk keep people productive through the polar night.

details.name: Snowdrift Boutique Hotel
details.purpose: A small boutique hotel on East Gallery Avenue for tourists who come to see the northern lights, visit the spa and explore downtown.
details.feature: A rooftop hot tub warmed by district-heating return water lets guests bathe under the aurora, and check-in is by phone key. The hotel lends thermal suits to visitors from warm countries and books aurora tours and spa passes at the desk.

details.name: [East Gallery Avenue] Street Lanterns, Snow Spruces & Street Life
details.purpose: The southern half of East Gallery Avenue, a lantern-lit street of shops and concert venues lined with snow spruces, busy with shoppers, concert-goers and a parked electric van.
details.feature: Snow-melting pavements, wind-sheltering spruces and lanterns that brighten for passers-by make the avenue pleasant even in the polar night. At weekends it hosts an outdoor winter design market under heated canopies.

details.name: Arctic Design Studio
details.purpose: A design studio and maker space where designers create polar clothing, furniture and building parts, and residents can join evening workshops.
details.feature: Its workshop 3D-prints furniture and building parts from recycled plastic and glassy slag from the Plasma Waste Converter, and every design is tested in a cold chamber at -50 °C before it goes on sale.

details.name: Fjord Furniture House
details.purpose: A furniture and home store on Glacier Avenue selling sofas, beds, rugs and insulating curtains for the city's flats and houses.
details.feature: It works as a circular store: old furniture is bought back, repaired in its workshop and sold again or donated. Insulating curtains and rugs sold here help homes save up to 15% of their heating.

details.name: Northern Lights Music Hall
details.purpose: A concert hall and community music school on East Gallery Avenue, for orchestra and choir concerts and music lessons for children and adults.
details.feature: Movable acoustic panels retune the hall for anything from a string quartet to a rock concert. Through the polar night it holds free lunchtime concerts, streamed live to Snowflake General Hospital and the city's senior homes.

details.name: Snow Lantern Primary School
details.purpose: A primary school for about 450 children aged 6 to 11 from the southern districts: Aurora 81 Residences, Snowpine Residences and the Mount Aurora Approach.
details.feature: Classrooms have daylight-spectrum lighting and lessons start later in the polar night. A heated rooftop play deck is used in any weather, pupils share the music hall next door for lessons and concerts, and every class practises the walk to the Residential Emergency Shelter each term.

details.name: Aurora Sports & Ski Shop
details.purpose: Sells skis, skates, snowshoes and warm sportswear and services equipment for residents, school teams and fans of the Aurora Snow Stadium.
details.feature: A cold chamber tests boots and gear at -45 °C before sale, and a fitting studio scans feet for a perfect fit. Outgrown children's gear is bought back and rented out cheaply, and skis are waxed with plant-based wax that does not harm the snow.

details.name: [East Gallery Avenue] Street Lanterns, Snow Spruces & Street Life
details.purpose: The southern half of East Gallery Avenue, a lantern-lit street of shops and concert venues lined with snow spruces, busy with shoppers, concert-goers and a parked electric van.
details.feature: Snow-melting pavements, wind-sheltering spruces and lanterns that brighten for passers-by make the avenue pleasant even in the polar night. At weekends it hosts an outdoor winter design market under heated canopies.

details.name: Snowpine Senior Care Home
details.purpose: A small, homely care home in Snowpine Residences for about 12 older residents who need daily support, with a day lounge for seniors who still live at home nearby.
details.feature: Step-free rooms, warm floors and fall sensors alert the nurses at once; daylight-spectrum lighting keeps body clocks steady through the polar night, and a video link to Snowflake General Hospital lets doctors check on residents without a trip through the cold.

details.name: Birch Lane House
details.purpose: A two-storey family home in Snowpine Residences for a family of four, a few minutes' walk from the kindergarten and the shops of the Mount Aurora Approach.
details.feature: Its steep roof sheds snow by itself, so it never has to be shovelled, and solar roof tiles charge a home battery that soaks up the 24-hour sunshine of the midnight-sun months.

details.name: Frostberry Home
details.purpose: A home in Snowpine Residences for a family that loves to cook and grow its own food.
details.feature: An LED-lit kitchen wall grows herbs, salad and strawberries all winter, and a food-scrap chute in the kitchen sends peelings to the city's biogas tank instead of the bin.

details.name: Northstar Townhouse
details.purpose: A narrow three-storey townhouse in Snowpine Residences for a young family, with a home office on the top floor.
details.feature: Its compact, tall shape has less outside wall to lose heat, and a heat-recovery ventilation unit keeps the air fresh while saving about 80% of the warmth that would otherwise escape.

details.name: Willow Snow House
details.purpose: A roomy detached house in Snowpine Residences for a busy household of five.
details.feature: A smart-home system learns the family's routine and warms each room only when it is used; in "blizzard mode" insulated shutters close by themselves when winds pass 90 km/h.

details.name: Aurora Family Home
details.purpose: A large multigenerational home in Snowpine Residences where grandparents, parents and children live together.
details.feature: A step-free ground-floor bedroom and bathroom suit the grandparents, and a heated boot room with drying racks and storage for e-bikes and sleds stops snow and cold from entering the living space.

details.name: Pinecone Kindergarten
details.purpose: The neighbourhood kindergarten and day nursery of Snowpine Residences, caring for about 40 children aged 1 to 6 while their parents work.
details.feature: Heated floors for crawling toddlers, a wind-sheltered snow playground with a warm-up hut, and daylight-spectrum classroom lights that keep children's sleep healthy through the polar night; parents drop off through a warm airlock entrance.

details.name: Icicle Cottage
details.purpose: A cosy cottage in Snowpine Residences for a retired couple.
details.feature: Despite its name it never grows icicles: heated gutters and a snow-melting front path stop dangerous ice from forming, so the couple can step out safely even on the darkest winter mornings.

details.name: Hearth House
details.purpose: A snug home in Snowpine Residences built around a warm living-room hearth.
details.feature: Instead of a wood fire, its hearth is a stone heat-storage wall charged by the district-heating loop at night, so the living room glows warm all day with zero smoke and no fuel burned.

details.name: Lumi House
details.purpose: A bright, light-filled home in Snowpine Residences whose name means "snow" in Finnish.
details.feature: Light tubes on the roof bring daylight deep into the house whenever the sun is up, and dawn-simulating lamps wake the family gently during the two months of polar night.

details.name: Cloudberry Cottage
details.purpose: A single-storey cottage in Snowpine Residences for a small family.
details.feature: A greywater system filters water from the shower and sink and reuses it to flush toilets, cutting the home's water use by about 40%, in step with the city's closed water loop.

details.name: Fjordview Home
details.purpose: A compact starter home in Snowpine Residences for a young couple.
details.feature: It stands on insulated piles above a ventilated air gap, so its warmth never thaws the permafrost below, and a small airlock porch keeps icy wind out each time the door opens.

details.name: [Snowpine Residences] Street Lanterns, Snow Spruces & Street Life
details.purpose: The heated sidewalks and shared courtyard of Snowpine Residences, with lanterns, snow spruces, log benches, a neighbourhood Christmas tree and children playing in the snow.
details.feature: Sidewalks warmed by district-heating return water stay snow-free, lanterns dim when the street is empty and brighten as someone walks by, and spruces shelter the courtyard from wind; two tame reindeer from the city's eco-tour herd visit the children each winter.

details.name: Mount Aurora Guesthouse
details.purpose: A family-run guesthouse with ten cosy rooms for tourists visiting the spa, on the boulevard leading to Mount Aurora.
details.feature: Every room has blackout blinds for the midnight-sun months and heated floors, a boot-drying room thaws wet gear overnight, and the spa pass sold at reception includes free rides on the spa shuttle.

details.name: Ski & Snowshoe Rental
details.purpose: Rents skis, snowshoes, sleds, ice skates and heated outdoor clothing to tourists and residents for trips around Mount Aurora and the tundra.
details.feature: Gear is booked online and collected from heated self-service lockers; every rental pack includes a GPS beacon that calls mountain rescue at the press of a button, and worn-out gear goes to the Circular Recycling Center.

details.name: Summit Gift Shop
details.purpose: Sells souvenirs of Mount Aurora and the city: aurora photo prints, local crafts, spa bath salts and mineral cosmetics from the geothermal springs.
details.feature: Most goods are made in Aurora Haven, including paperweights cast from the glassy stone of the Plasma Waste Converter, and everything is wrapped in recycled paper with zero plastic.

details.name: Alpine Hot Pot
details.purpose: A hot-pot restaurant where families and skiers share steaming pots of broth after a cold day, open late through the polar night.
details.feature: Induction plates powered by clean electricity heat every table, so no gas burns indoors; broths use mushrooms and greens from the Evergreen greenhouse domes and protein from the Snow-to-Food plant, and food scraps go to the Biogas Tank.

details.name: Spa Shuttle Lodge
details.purpose: The heated waiting lodge and stop for the electric spa shuttle, which loops between the downtown metro, the guesthouses on the Approach and the North Portal of Mount Aurora.
details.feature: Driverless electric shuttles run every 5 minutes and recharge wirelessly at the stop; live screens show the next arrival and how busy the spa is, and the warm waiting room keeps guests out of the -45 °C wind.

details.name: Base Camp Café
details.purpose: A cosy café for coffee, hot chocolate and pastries where walkers, spa guests and neighbours warm up.
details.feature: Drinks come in deposit mugs that can be returned anywhere in the city, heat from the ovens and coffee machines warms the room, and in a blizzard its warm-up corner stays open 24 hours as a public warming point.

details.name: Ama Dablam Outfitters
details.purpose: Sells and repairs polar clothing and mountain gear: down parkas, heated gloves, crampons and snow boots built for -45 °C.
details.feature: A cold-test chamber lets shoppers try clothes at -40 °C before buying, and a repair workshop fixes zips, soles and heated liners so gear lasts for years instead of being thrown away.

details.name: [Mount Aurora Approach] Street Lanterns, Snow Spruces & Street Life
details.purpose: The walking street of the Mount Aurora Approach, where tourists stroll under lanterns and snow spruces between the guesthouses, the shops and the spa shuttle.
details.feature: Every building on the street is kept low so the summit stays in view; kerbside chargers top up the few electric cars, rows of spruces break the wind for walkers, and the lanterns use warm, low-glare light that does not hide the aurora.

details.name: Glacier View Inn
details.purpose: A small boutique inn whose rooms face Mount Aurora's hanging glacier, for couples and visitors staying several nights at the spa.
details.feature: Glass-roofed loft rooms let guests watch the northern lights from bed, and smart room controls turn the district heating down the moment guests leave and back up before they return.

details.name: Hot Spring Supply Store
details.purpose: Sells swimwear, thermal robes, waterproof bags, bath salts and mineral skincare for visitors heading to the spa and the Aurora Lagoon.
details.feature: Its bath salts and silica clay come from the spa's own geothermal springs in refillable jars; visitors who forgot their kit can rent towels and swimwear and drop them in a return chute at the North Portal.

details.name: Southside Police & Mountain Rescue Post
details.purpose: The community police station of the southern district and base of a small mountain-rescue team, looking after Snowpine Residences, the Mount Aurora Approach and spa visitors.
details.feature: Officers patrol on electric snowmobiles and e-bikes, a heated garage keeps a tracked rescue vehicle ready 24 hours a day, and the post is linked to the Polar Rescue and Resilience Station; it also runs the district's first-aid point and lost-and-found.

details.name: Sherpa Tea House
details.purpose: A Himalayan-style tea house serving butter tea, masala chai, dumplings and soup, named after the Sherpa mountain guides of Nepal.
details.feature: Teas are brewed with mineral water from the Snow-to-Food & Water Plant, and a tea terrace with infrared heaters run on clean electricity lets guests sit outside and gaze at the summit even in deep winter.

details.name: Snowline Mountain Guides
details.purpose: Certified guides lead snowshoe hikes, ice climbing on the hanging glacier, tundra treks and night-time aurora walks for tourists and residents.
details.feature: Every group carries satellite trackers watched by the Southside Police & Mountain Rescue Post, guides check live weather and snow sensors before each trip, and free winter-safety courses teach residents how to survive a blizzard.

details.name: Aurora Photo Studio
details.purpose: A photo studio and gallery that runs northern-lights photography tours, takes family portraits and prints photos of visitors in front of Mount Aurora.
details.feature: An aurora forecast feed from the Aurora Observatory alerts tour groups the moment the lights appear, and prints use recycled paper and plant-based inks.
